payload.claim: `_over_budget` compares `spent` (initialized to `0.0` at line 1788, unconditionally, even when `spec.task_id` is given) against `spec.budget_usd`. `spent` only accumulates cost from turns run inside *this* cell invocation. Before this change every cell minted a fresh task, so that was the task's whole spend; now a task can be handed back across a SPEC_REVIEW/SPEC_WRITING attempt and one or more prior RATE_LIMITED cell runs on the same `task_id` (the exact scenario this diff adds), and none of that prior spend is added in here. DESIGN.md's spend-axis row says the supervisor 'sums reported cost against task ... ceilings', but on a reused task this check only ever sees the current invocation's own tally, so a task can be re-admitted for a full `budget_usd` allowance on every rerun instead of being charged cumulatively. Criterion 2 fixes this same gap for the *reported* `spent_usd`/`spent_usd_est` by subtracting `start_spend`, but the live `_over_budget` ceiling used to trip `EXHAUSTED` (here and at lines 2129, 2343, 2415, 2731) was never updated to add `start_spend` back in, so the actual spend ceiling enforced for a reused task is silently weaker than `spec.budget_usd` states.
